default: Unknown control; unnamed land does not establish absence of settlement.

references.title: National Museum of Natural Science, Millennium Pottery Techniques

namedFeatures.decision: An approximate Neolithic cultural layer fits the period; preserve the source's BP dating rather than claiming exact Gregorian endpoints. The museum supplies no ruler or island-wide frontier. Do not interpret `PARTOF: Dakapeng culture` as sovereign authority.

namedFeatures.decision: Reject the supplied broad Island Southeast Asian distribution as a verified 3000 BC snapshot. references.title: National Museum of Australia, The Black Line

namedFeatures.decision: Indigenous presence predates 3000 BC. Use a broad explanatory label with local identity unresolved; no island-wide monarch or 3000 BC clan boundaries follow. Do not apply colonial population counts to the bookmark.

namedFeatures.evidence: [UNESCO decision 44 COM 8B.37](https://whc.unesco.org/en/decisions/7956/), adopted Statement of Outstanding Universal Value, dates northern Japanese sedentary hunter-fisher-gatherer development about **13,000–400 BCE**.
namedFeatures.decision: Supports an archaeological culture around 3000 BC. The serial sites do not certify this polygon's extent or one Jōmon state. Review its division from the adjacent Ainu-labeled region separately.

namedFeatures.evidence: [UNESCO, Sacred City of Caral-Supe](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1269), description / Brief synthesis / Integrity, discusses multiple urban settlements and dates development **3000–1800 BC**.
namedFeatures.decision: Supports local Caral-Supe society and hierarchy, not a single documented king of the polygon called Norte Chico. The oldest endpoint remains approximate. Do not treat a modern site's World Heritage boundary as the ancient political frontier.

namedFeatures.evidence: [The Met, Eastern Mediterranean and Syria, 8000–2000 BC](https://www.metmuseum.org/it/toah/ht/02/wae), Overview, describes local city-state development during the **third millennium BC**.

references.title: The Met, Eastern Mediterranean and Syria, 8000–2000 BC

namedFeatures.decision: Plausible regional process, but the generic label neither identifies constituent polities nor fixes the configuration at 3000 BC. Research settlements separately; no common ruler or umbrella state.

namedFeatures.evidence: [French Ministry of Culture, Ur](https://archeologie.culture.gouv.fr/en/glossary/ur), opening entry, identifies Tell Muqqayar and occupation from the fifth millennium. [Penn Museum B17008](https://collections.penn.museum/collections/object/232090), Date Made / Description, catalogs an Ur grave object around **3000 BCE**; its register transcription instead says circa **3100 BC**.
namedFeatures.decision: Accept a local Ur setting with explicit chronological uncertainty. **Do not approve the whole upstream Ur polygon as Ur's state**: the earlier containment audit places Uruk inside it. Later royal tombs and Ur III do not establish 3000 BC imperial authority. No exact-year ruler sourced.

namedFeatures.evidence: [Robert K. Englund, Encyclopaedia Iranica, Proto-Elamite](https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/elam-iii/), opening paragraphs, dates the writing system around **3050–2900 BCE** and identifies administrative centers across Susiana and the Iranian highlands. The precursor language remains unknown.

references.title: Robert K. Englund, Encyclopaedia Iranica, Proto-Elamite

namedFeatures.decision: Supports a **Proto-Elamite administrative/cultural** setting. It does not validate one kingdom called Elam covering this polygon in 3000 BC. Keep the political claim unresolved; do not turn shared accounting practice into sovereignty or silently rename the feature.

namedFeatures.evidence: [du Plessis, The linguistic classification of Kora](https://sahistory.org.za/archive/kora-lost-khoisan-language-early-cape-and-gariep-menan-du-plessis-1-linguistic), linguistic-family discussion, distinguishes groupings and uncertain histories. references.title: du Plessis, The linguistic classification of Kora

namedFeatures.decision: Preserve uncertainty about 3000 BC identity and distribution. Do not equate a modern umbrella term, language families, subsistence and one political unit. These sources do not validate the polygon across southern/eastern Africa.

namedFeatures.evidence: [Egyptian Ministry, Early Dynastic Period](https://egymonuments.gov.eg/historical-periods/early-dynastic-period/), date heading and first paragraphs, gives about **3100–2686 BC**, gradual unification and Memphis as capital. [NMEC timeline](https://nmec.gov.eg/historical-timeline/), Archaic Period, corroborates the state/capital.
namedFeatures.decision: Recommended playable state around 3000 BC with a generated household. Use the disclosed approximate upstream frontier and the companion report's qualified Memphis marker. No exact-year king or exact frontier approved here.

namedFeatures.evidence: [Yale eHRAF, Early Indus summary](https://ehrafarchaeology.yale.edu/traditions/aq43/summary), identification / temporal coverage, distinguishes Early Harappan/Regionalization traditions. namedFeatures.decision: Retain an **Early Harappan** cultural context; exact placement at the 3000 BC boundary and the large polygon require review. Do not backdate the mature urban system or invent an Indus monarch, deciphered royal title or family tree.

namedFeatures.evidence: [Gernot Wilhelm, Hurrian, Cambridge](https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/abs/ancient-languages-of-asia-minor/hurrian/190C6E806AD18A753663423855472264), chapter summary, places first attestations in Akkade-period words/names, **23rd–22nd centuries BC**, and wider evidence in the last quarter of the third millennium.
namedFeatures.decision: Reject this precise political aggregate as a researched 3000 BC map label. Later attestations do not prove an earlier population absent; they also do not source its kingdoms at this date. Keep the earlier political configuration unknown.

namedFeatures.evidence: [Textile Museum of Canada / Gardiner Museum, Artifact 8](https://textilemuseum.ca/cloth_clay/resources/intermediate_08-2.html), WHO/WHERE/WHEN, gives Valdivia, southern coastal Ecuador and **3200–1500 BC**. namedFeatures.decision: Supports a local ceramic tradition around the bookmark. Ritual interpretations are qualified hypotheses. No Ecuador-wide political unity or ruler follows; the upstream extent remains unverified.

namedFeatures.evidence: [Kerma archaeological mission, Pre-Kerma agglomeration](https://kerma.ch/pre-kerma-agglomeration/), final paragraph, dates **Pre-Kerma 3500–2500 BC** and states that territorial extent and social organization remain difficult to establish. namedFeatures.decision: Reject an unqualified Kerma kingdom/city-state label for 3000 BC. A separate **Pre-Kerma** cultural record is defensible; its boundaries and political organization need research. No automatic relabeling of the existing political polygon.

namedFeatures.evidence: [Sereno et al., PLOS ONE, Gobero](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0002995), mid-Holocene subsistence discussion, describes **5200–2500 BCE** local combinations of fishing, wild resources and domestic cattle. references.title: Sereno et al., PLOS ONE, Gobero

namedFeatures.decision: This is a generic subsistence description, not a people or government. The wide multi-part feature includes Madagascar; its 3000 BC population cannot be inferred from the label. Keep regional identities, occupation and control unresolved rather than asserting uniform foragers.
